title: GeoTrackV1
description: One geographically-located thing a sensor currently reports, in a form a map can draw without further lookup. Published per-track under <prefix>/geo/track/<sensor>/<uid>. Provenance is structural: producer_anchor is the key's own first chunk, admitted by the router ACL. This is a DISPLAY schema, deliberately not a sensor-interchange standard: the interchange formats are what edge gateways emit (ASTERIX CAT-62, CoT, ISA, SAPIENT), and this is what those are reduced to once the enum lookups have been resolved.

schema.description: Version is a first-class field; subscribers gate on it.

id.description: Stable identity, '<sensor>:<sensor-uid>'. Unique across sensors on one fabric.

label.description: What to draw next to the dot — the raw sensor uid, not the namespaced id.

kind.description: From the topic leaf, not the payload. The map draws the two differently.

node.description: Edge node that produced the canonical, e.g. gateway-001.

alt_m.description: Height above ellipsoid, metres. null = not reported.

course_deg.description: Degrees true. null means NOT REPORTED and is distinct from 0, which means due north.

speed_mps.description: Metres per second. null means NOT REPORTED and is distinct from 0, which means stationary.

ce_m.description: Circular error, metres. CoT's 9999999 'no usable estimate' sentinel is normalised to null so a consumer never draws a 10 000 km error circle.

le_m.description: Linear (vertical) error, metres. Same sentinel handling as ce_m.

cot_type.description: Originating CoT type string, carried for traceability. Consumers should read affiliation/dimension instead of re-parsing this.

affiliation.description: Resolved from the CoT affiliation letter. Unrecognised letters degrade to 'unknown' rather than failing the record.

dimension.description: Resolved from the CoT battle-dimension letter.

how.description: CoT 'how' — provenance of the position (measured, estimated, ...).

descriptor.description: Free-text description from the sensor chain, e.g. the CoT detail/uid string.

reported_at.description: The SENSOR's own clock, verbatim and unrepaired. MAY BE WRONG — a sensor chain with an unset clock reports 1970. Never use for staleness or ordering; never silently correct it, because a repaired timestamp is indistinguishable from a real one downstream.

stale_at.description: Sensor-declared staleness horizon. Same trust caveat as reported_at.

observed_at.description: When the producer received the bytes. This is the trustworthy clock and the one every age, fade and TTL is computed from.

trail.description: Recent positions, oldest first, as [lon, lat] pairs — GeoJSON axis order. Added by the producer's store, not present in the sensor payload.

updates.description: How many messages have contributed to this track since the producer first saw it.

first_seen_at.description: observed_at of the first message for this id.

synthetic.description: TRUE means this track is simulated and must never be mistaken for a real detection. Set from the producer org's registry `synthetic` flag, not self-declared in the payload, so a real producer cannot accidentally (or deliberately) mark itself notional or vice versa. Renderers MUST mark synthetic tracks distinctly; a viewer who cannot tell simulation from reality is worse off than one with no map.

producer_anchor.description: The 32-hex slot anchor that published this track — the FIRST chunk of the Zenoh key it arrived on. Structural, not asserted: the router's ACL only admits writes under a peer's own anchor, so this cannot be forged by the payload. This is the key `data.view.producer:<anchor>` scopes on (ADR 1074).

org.description: Display name of the producing org, resolved from the registry for humans. NEVER an access-control input — scoping keys on producer_anchor, because ownership is mutable and names are not identities (ADR 1051: cert = born-as, registry = currently-is).
